<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par152 />{{GHGmargin-letter|152|x}}
(''k'') {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי|translate=that... not}}, with the imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=14}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=14}} read the infinitive {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּב}} for {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫בוּ}}, in 27:8 {{GHGheb|text=יָבֹ֫אוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫אוּ}}). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי רָאוּ}} is a relative clause governed by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}= ''according to'' things which ''they have not seen''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|y}}
'''2.''' Two negatives in the same sentence do not neutralize each other (as in ''nonnulli, non nemo''), but make the negation the more emphatic (like οὐκ οὐδείς, οὐκ οὐδαμῶς, ''nulli—non, nemo non''); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=2|verse=2}} (if the text is correct) {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם לֹֽא־יָבוֹא|translate=before there shall}} (not) ''come''.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵין־כֶּ֫סֶף}} goes with what precedes and must be emended, with the LXX and Lucian, to {{GHGheb|text=כִּי הַכֶּ֫סֶף}}.</ref> This especially applies to the compounds formed by the union of {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} or {{GHGheb|text=בְּלִי}} with {{GHGheb|text=מִן־|translate=without}} ({{GHGpar|119|y}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=9}} (6:11) {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵין יוֹשֵׁב}} (for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=מִבְּלִי יֹשֵׁב}}), prop. ''without no inhabitant'', i.e. ''so that no inhabitant is left there''. On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵין מַ֫יִם}} the {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} is causative, ''because there is no water''; as also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲמִבְּלִי אֵין־|translate=is it because there were no...?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=1|verse=3}}, 6, 16. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=מִבְּלִי אֲשֶׁר לֹא|translate=except that}} (''yet so that man cannot'', &c.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|z}}
'''3.''' The negative sometimes extends its influence from the first to a second negative sentence parallel with it (which may or may not have {{GHGterm|Wāw}}); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=3}} ''talk not so much arrogancy''; ''let'' (not) ''boasting come out of your mouth''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=22|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, 15 f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=27|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=47}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=13|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=75|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=17}} (so {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה לֹא|translate=why... not?}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=11}} also affects the parallel clause).<section end=par152 />

<section begin=par153 />{{GHGpar-heading|153|Restrictive and Intensive Clauses}}

The particles {{GHGheb|text=אַךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַק|translate=only}}, serve to introduce restrictive clauses, and {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַף|translate=also, besides, even}}, intensive clauses. It is to be observed that the force of these particles does not necessarily affect the word which immediately follows (as is the case with {{GHGheb|text=אַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=15|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=רַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=2}}; even {{GHGheb|text=הֲרַק אַךְ|translate=hath he indeed only?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=12|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=17}}), but very frequently extends to the whole of the following sentence. Thus with {{GHGheb|text=אַךְ}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=6|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=רַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=21|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=גַּם הִנֵּה}}), 44:10; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=11|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=4|hidebook=1}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=1|verse=10}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=2|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} is placed before two co-ordinate sentences, although, strictly speaking, it applies only to the second. Cf. the analogous examples in {{GHGpar|150|m}}.<section end=par153 /><noinclude>
